omissions.explanation: The client removes ApiVersionPolicy and adds ClientApiVersionPolicy, which appends the configured API version when URLSearchParams.get("api-version") returns a falsy value, including when the parameter is absent or has an empty value.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: A bespoke request-pipeline policy is present in the client context, but this evidence is marked unknown and provides no generated counterpart; whether it was handwritten is unresolved.

omissions.subtype: Local AES-CBC encrypt and decrypt provider
omissions.explanation: The AES provider performs local AES-CBC encryption and decryption with Node crypto, chooses an IV for encryption when none is supplied, checks algorithm and operation support, and validates the symmetric key type and minimum key length.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: A dedicated cryptography provider directly invokes Node crypto and maintains its own AES algorithm table outside the repetitive REST operation module; the evidence kind is unknown and no generated counterpart was supplied, so provenance is not conclusive.

omissions.subtype: RSA public JWK to PEM conversion
omissions.explanation: The conversion function DER-encodes an RSA JWK's modulus and exponent, base64-encodes the sequence, and wraps it as an RSA public-key PEM string.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: This cryptography helper explicitly implements DER and PEM encoding outside the REST operation module; the evidence kind is unknown and no generated counterpart was supplied, so its provenance remains unconfirmed.

omissions.explanation: The hashing helper maps supported signature algorithm names to SHA digest algorithms, rejects unmapped names, and computes the digest locally through Node crypto.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The helper contains an explicit signature-to-digest mapping and local Node crypto call rather than a generated wire operation; its evidence kind is unknown and no generated counterpart confirms provenance.

omissions.explanation: The verifier helper maps signature algorithms to SHA digest algorithms, rejects unsupported names, and initializes a Node crypto verifier with the supplied data.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The helper configures a local Node crypto verifier using an explicit algorithm map rather than a REST operation; its evidence kind is unknown and no generated counterpart confirms provenance.

limitations: Coverage is partial: eight distinct source paths of 49 eligible files are supplied, including only lines 1-731 of api/operations.ts. Public key and cryptography clients, LRO implementations, remote/RSA providers, models, transformations and paging/URL helpers are excluded. Empty findings do not establish absence of package customizations.

All eight evidence items have unknown provenance. No generated counterpart, overlay comparison, customization-folder marker, explicit handwritten attribution or generation ownership map is supplied. The frozen JavaScript guideline explicitly leaves provenance in modular src layouts unresolved; local algorithm complexity, missing generated headers and src/cryptography placement alone are not treated as definitive proof of handwriting.

The concrete local AES candidate implements encrypt/decrypt using Node crypto, an optional or random 16-byte encryption IV, and A128CBCPAD/A192CBCPAD/A256CBCPAD mappings. ensureValid checks OCT/OCT-HSM type, key material and a minimum key size, then the operations use the selected prefix of key bytes. isSupported checks key presence, algorithm membership and operation membership but does not itself perform the type/length checks. No public-client selection, browser behavior or complete local-to-remote fallback is shown.

The AES provider also throws an imported LocalCryptographyUnsupportedError for wrap, unwrap, sign, signData, verify and verifyData. The error implementation and callers that might catch it are excluded; the supplied declarations do not prove a working fallback or show which library generator owns this provider.

The conversion-module candidate encodes RSA modulus/exponent bytes through local DER-length/buffer/sequence helpers and formats RSA PUBLIC KEY PEM with 64-character base64 lines. It rejects missing modulus/exponent and oversized encoded lengths. This is observable local conversion logic, not proof of generated-versus-handwritten provenance or standards conformance; only the two-part RSA call site is supplied.

The crypto helper candidate maps ES/PS/RS signature algorithm names to SHA256/SHA384/SHA512 and rejects unmapped names before using Node hash or verifier creation. createVerify updates and ends a verifier but does not itself test a signature; randomBytes directly delegates to the platform helper. Imported provider interfaces, RSA consumers and broader runtime use are absent.

createKeyVault visibly configures endpoint precedence, user-agent/logging/scope options and API version, removes ApiVersionPolicy and adds ClientApiVersionPolicy. Its policy appends a configured version when the parsed URL has no truthy api-version value. With no generated comparison or customization signal, this client-factory/policy scaffold is not promoted to a handwritten API-version or authentication finding.

The captured operation send/deserialize pairs construct protocol requests, deserialize expected responses and attach deserialized service errors; getDeletedKeys calls buildPagedAsyncIterator with value/nextLink names. These bodies resemble normal generated operations and have no affirmative handwritten signal. The paging helper is excluded, and no custom next-link handling, cryptographic wire implementation or polling behavior is inferred from names, imports, service descriptions or dependencies.

api/index.ts only re-exports operations/types; empty option interfaces and the SDK_VERSION constant do not independently demonstrate customized runtime behavior. Package dependencies such as core-lro are not evidence of an LRO customization, and the actual excluded delete/recover pollers remain unassessed.

The frozen moduleMajor identity is 1 while package source reports 4.11.0-beta.2 and latestRelease metadata reports 4.11.0-beta.1. This review neither reconciles that identity/version mismatch nor verifies a released artifact, compiler output, network behavior or cryptographic execution.
No analyst proposals were supplied; the five omissions are candidate behaviors only, remain inconclusive, and cannot be counted as accepted customizations.

Coverage is partial: 8 of 49 eligible source files were captured; operations.ts ends at line 731 and 21 skipped entries include client, crypto, transformation, paging, models, and LRO sources. This review cannot establish package-wide absence or completeness.

Every source evidence item is marked unknown, with no generated counterpart or explicit provenance for the candidate modules; whether these behaviors are handwritten remains unresolved. The repetitive REST operations and paging wrapper alone do not establish customization.
